text:
alex: Quick async check-in for today — API gateway / routing / auth / rate limits

alex: Yesterday — finished integration tests for the new routing policy matcher, validated shadow traffic for svc-b via the staging gateway. Observed baseline 95th latency ~120ms (no regressions).

alex: Blockers — seeing a small surge of 429s when we enable the new rate rule in the canary namespace, unclear if it's a token-bucket mis-config or client behavior.

maggie: saw the 429 spike in logs too, +1 on token-bucket mystery. I can help pull detailed logs from the ingress LB. :mag:

ravi: I ran a quick sim this morning — when we set burst to 50 and refill 10/s for that route, bursts from async clients can still push us over. Might need a lower burst or smoother refill.

sam: ping @alex — I left comments on your PR (router matcher) about the wildcard precedence. quick note: please add a small unit test for overlapping rules. :eyes:

alex: thanks @sam, will add tests. @maggie if you grab LB logs can you include client-id header samples? suspecting a handful of clients hitting retries.

maggie: will do, pulling logs now. found a couple of clients with aggressive retry backoff missing. sending sample in a sec.

lee: FYI I pushed a tiny tweak to auth middleware to short-circuit expired tokens earlier. shouldn't affect routing but reduced CPU on the edge by ~3% in local bench.

ravi: good to know. if auth short-circuit reduces window for rate accounting we should double-check metrics alignment (tokens consumed vs requests accepted).

alex: plan for today — 1) add the router PR test and respond to @sam comments, 2) pair with @maggie on LB logs and correlate client-ids to 429s, 3) try an interim rate tweak: burst 30 refill 12/s in canary and observe for 1 hour, 4) if stable, promote to next canary.

maggie: logs show ~12 client-ids responsible for ~70% of 429s, many are retrying every 200-300ms. I'll open a small ticket to contact the teams.

sam: quick QA ask — when you flip the canary rule, can we add a temporary tracing tag like `x-gw-canary-v2` so we can filter traces?

alex: yep will add `x-gw-canary: v2` header to routed requests in canary mode. good call.

ravi: suggestion — consider soft-deny header for high-volume clients with advice to slow down, rather than hard 429 immediately. we can return `Retry-After` + guidance.

alex: noted. will prototype soft-deny behaviour once we stabilise the rule.

deploy-bot: deploy scheduled: canary-config-update to gw-canary at 2026-03-18T15:40Z (dry-run mode). :robot_face:

maggie: thanks bot — I'll watch logs during the dry run.

sam: thumbs up — will do a quick smoke after you add the trace header. :thumbsup:

alex: thanks all. will post a short follow-up here after the 1-hour observation window.
